LESSON: WRITING 4.4.1 HANDWRITING BRAILLE WRITING

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.4: Writing 4.4.1 Handwriting Braille writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 4.4.1 Handwriting Braille writing, part of Strand 4 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why do we write neatly and legibly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 4.4.1 Handwriting Braille writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration: The learner’s ability to write clearly and correctly is improved as they write words in clear and legible handwriting

or braille writing.

Values:
Respect is enhanced as the learner works together with peers to write neat and legible sentences.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (Self-esteem): The learner’s self-esteem is nurtured as their handwriting improves through practise in writing neatly and legibly.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner is able to use the aspects of good handwriting in learning of similar concept in Kiswahili Language Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

• Print textbooks in appropriate font size and colour contrast

• Braille books

• Digital devices with assistive technology,

• Charts, flash cards or braille cards,

• Pictures or picture description
